descriptionChirho: A city east of the Jordan, residence of Og king of Bashan (Deut 1:4; Josh 9:10, 12:4, 13:12,31), later assigned to the Levites (1 Chr 6:71). The name derives from the worship of the goddess Ashtart at this location; attested in Egyptian records as 'astartu'. Used with various prepositions: בְּעַשְׁתָּרֹת 'in Ashtaroth' (Deut 1:4; Josh 9:10, 12:4, 13:12). All languages transliterate uniformly: Arabic عَشْتاروتَ, Korean 아스다롯, Hindi अश्तारोत, Spanish Astarot/Astarot. This sense is the geographic proper noun referring to the specific Transjordanian city.

The plural form referring to Ashtaroth/Astarte goddesses or their cult images, Canaanite fertility deities worshipped alongside the Baals. Israel served the Ashtaroth in the period of the Judges (Judg 2:13, 10:6; 1 Sam 7:3-4, 12:10), and Samuel called for their removal (1 Sam 7:3). Often paired with הַבְּעָלִים (the Baals) as a stock phrase for Canaanite idolatry. Typically has the article (הָעַשְׁתָּרוֹת) when denoting the goddesses generically. Spanish distinctively uses 'las Astartés/las Ashtarot' (plural feminine), Korean uses 아스다롯들 (with plural marker), and Arabic uses the article الـعَشتاروتَ. This religious/cultic sense is distinct from the geographic proper noun.
